T: A spoonful of sugar. Then a full plate.
D: A magical nanny arrives at Cherry Tree Lane to look after the Banks children.
P: Serve the snacks when Uncle Albert's tea party floats up to the ceiling.
S: the tea party on the ceiling with Uncle Albert
Finger sandwiches of cucumber and cream cheese, egg and cress, and ham and mustard, crusts off, on a tiered plate.
the bird woman selling crumbs on the steps of St Paul's

Crunchy seeded crackers of sunflower, pumpkin, linseed and sesame, baked thin, with whipped goat's cheese, honey and cracked pepper. Mix 60g sunflower seeds, 60g pepitas, 40g linseeds, 40g sesame seeds and 30g rolled oats with 1 tbsp chia seeds, 1/2 tsp salt and 200ml boiling water. Rest 15 minutes until thick, then spread thinly between 2 sheets of baking paper. Peel off the top sheet and bake at 160C for 1 hour until crisp, then snap into shards. Whip 150g soft goat's cheese with 2 tbsp milk and serve with honey and pepper.

Golden crimped pastry half-moons packed with peppery beef, potato, swede and onion, baked until the juices bubble, with brown sauce. Mix 400g finely diced chuck steak with 250g diced potato, 150g diced swede, 1 diced onion, 1 tsp salt and plenty of pepper. Cut 4 x 20cm rounds from 4 sheets of shortcrust pastry. Pile the filling onto one half of each, dot with butter, fold over and crimp the edge. Brush with beaten egg, cut a small slit and bake at 200C for 15 minutes, then 170C for 40 minutes. Serve with brown sauce.
M: Sunday at the Banks house on Cherry Tree Lane
Beef topside roasted at 200C to medium, rested, with Yorkshire puddings, roast potatoes, peas and gravy.
Old London pie and mash with parsley sauce
the rooftops and streets of old London

Minced beef and onion pies in crisp pastry, with buttery mash and a bright green parsley sauce poured over, the London eel shop way. Brown 600g beef mince with 1 diced onion, add 1 tbsp plain flour, 300ml beef stock and pepper, and simmer 20 minutes until thick, then cool. Line 4 pie tins with shortcrust, fill and top with puff pastry. Brush with egg and bake at 200C for 25 minutes. Mash 1kg potatoes with butter. Melt 30g butter, stir in 2 tbsp flour, whisk in 400ml stock and simmer, then add a bunch of chopped parsley.
W: Mary and Bert jumping into the chalk pavement drawing

Raspberries blended with sugar syrup and lemon, frozen and scraped every hour until fluffy, served in glass dishes with wafers. Dissolve 150g sugar in 150ml hot water and cool. Blend 500g raspberries with the syrup and the juice of a lemon, then strain out the seeds. Freeze in a tray, scraping with a fork every hour for 4 hours. Serve in glass dishes with ice cream wafers.
K: Admiral Boom firing his cannon from the rooftop on Cherry Tree Lane

Fiery ginger and lemon syrup topped with fizzing soda over ice, with a sugar rim and a strip of candied ginger, served on the hour. Simmer 100g caster sugar, 100ml water and a 6cm piece of sliced ginger for 10 minutes, then cool and strain. Rub the rims of 4 glasses with lemon and dip in caster sugar. Fill with ice and add 3 tbsp ginger syrup and the juice of a quarter lemon to each. Top with soda water and stir. Garnish with a strip of crystallised ginger.

m.note: Sunday at the Banks house on Cherry Tree Lane
m.how: Roast a 1.5kg beef topside at 200C to medium and rest. Whisk 150g flour, 3 eggs and 300ml milk into a batter and bake in hot oiled muffin tins for 20 minutes. Roast 1kg potatoes alongside, cook peas and make gravy with pan juices and stock.
